# Running your app outside of jupyter notebook
- a handful of students cant display their solara dashboard in jupyter notebook
- well find a solution

# Solution: Run the solara dashboard from your terminal
VS Code has a built-in terminal (`Ctrl+ or View → Terminal`). We can run solara on your `.ipynb`. It will check where you call page and open a new tab in your browser with the solara dashboard.

```bash
conda activate mesa-env
solara run notebook_name.ipynb
```

If you want to autorestart when you edit the notebook, you can add the `--autoreload` flag:
```bash
solara run your_notebook.ipynb --auto-restart
```

# Some further tinkering with models

# Grid Model Questions (Open Question)
Lets say we now want to have the agents be able to move to any patch surrounding the current patch, including the diagonals. What would you change in python mesa grid model?

# Grid, network,  Model Questions (Use your own imagination)
Make a copy of the models. And try to think of a simple thing you can add that make your model behave slightly more interesting from your perspective. You can try to implement the change both in Netlogo and in Python.

# Fire model (Open Question)
Open the fire python mesa model. There is no dashboard. It just collects and plots some data from a running model. Could you implement a solaraviz however, based on what the basic models look like?
